test_title: PYST 41: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 01 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Directive Principles of State Policy is provided under Article 40 of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Promotion of cottage industries in rural areas
Provision for a uniform civil code
Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry

solution:
The correct answer is __**Organisation of village panchayats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 40 of the Indian Constitution** is a part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) and directs the state to take steps to organize **village panchayats** and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.
 
• The **concept of village panchayats** is deeply rooted in Indian history and tradition, emphasizing grassroots democracy and self-governance.
 
• The inclusion of Article 40 in the Constitution reflects the vision of the framers to ensure decentralized governance in India. *Hence, the correct answer is Article 40 focuses on the organisation of village panchayats.*
 
• The establishment of village panchayats forms a critical part of the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**, which institutionalized the Panchayati Raj system in India.
 
• Article 40 essentially serves as a guideline for states to empower rural governance and promote participatory democracy at the local level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy:**

 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are **guidelines or principles** given to the central and state governments of India to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are provided in **Part IV of the Indian Constitution** (Articles 36 to 51) and aim to establish a social and economic democracy in the country.
 
 
 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:**
 
 
• This act added **Part IX** to the Constitution, titled "The Panchayats," covering Articles 243 to 243O.
 
• It also added the **Eleventh Schedule** to the Constitution, which contains the functional items of the Panchayats (29 items).
 
• **Key Features:** Mandatory constitution of panchayats at the village, intermediate, and district levels; fixed tenure of five years; reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Village Panchayats:**
 
 
• Village panchayats are instrumental in promoting **decentralization**, ensuring people’s participation in decision-making, and fostering socio-economic development at the grassroots level.
 
• They are responsible for implementing government schemes, maintaining basic infrastructure, and addressing local issues.
 
• They also act as a platform for resolving disputes and maintaining harmony in rural areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Relevant Directive Principles:**

 
 
• **Promotion of cottage industries in rural areas** (Article 43): Encourages the state to promote village and small-scale industries to ensure rural development and self-sufficiency.
 
• **Provision for a uniform civil code** (Article 44): Directs the state to secure a uniform civil code for all citizens across India, ensuring equality and secularism.
 
• **Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry** (Article 48): Promotes modern and scientific methods to improve agriculture and animal welfare in India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Directive Principles:**
 
 
• They provide a framework for establishing a **welfare state**.
 
• Although non-justiciable, they act as a guiding force for the government to enact laws and policies aimed at socio-economic justice.
